description: Trigger discrimination: unattributed time/memory investigation design (this skill) vs functional root-cause (systematic-debugger), an evidenced single query (query-plan-reader), chatty data access (n-plus-one-detector), standing telemetry (observability-operator), pass/fail measurement (performance-test-harness), and forward-looking capacity/noisy-neighbor load planning (load-test-planner).

cases.prompt: Our nightly reconciliation got 40% slower after the ORM upgrade, but only in production; staging runs are flat. Nobody knows whether it's the queries, GC, or waiting on the file store. Do we reproduce it under load in staging or capture during a production window, and how do we narrow it down?
cases.note: SEAM CASE — 'reproduce under load' and 'production window' echo the load plan's staging-versus-production choice. Here the choice serves attributing a slowdown, not validating capacity.
cases.reason: profiling-methodology-designer's description covers 'why something is slow with no evidenced suspect', profiler classes including 'off-CPU/blocking-IO', measurement conditions ('warm vs cold, representative load and data volume'), 'the hypothesis-driven narrowing loop', and 'never runs profilers against production (approval-gated)'. load-test-planner is for 'capacity validation, or noisy-neighbor verification'. Neither is requested.

cases.prompt: Next month we onboard a tenant ten times bigger than anyone else. Design the test that proves the other tenants' latency doesn't suffer when that tenant runs its month-end import, with production-shaped data volumes and a stated blast radius.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse direction) — 'latency doesn't suffer' reads like a performance investigation. Nothing is slow yet, though. The ask is a forward-looking noisy-neighbour load scenario.
cases.reason: load-test-planner's description covers 'the noisy-neighbor scenario where one tenant's burst must not degrade the rest, judged per-tenant, not aggregate', 'data volumes seeded to production shape and skew', and 'blast radius stated per scenario'. profiling-methodology-designer answers 'where does the time (or memory) actually go' for an existing slowdown, and there is none here.

cases.prompt: Everything about the export job feels slow but nobody can say whether it's the queries, the transformation code, or writing the output — design how we find out where the time goes.
cases.reason: No evidenced suspect exists — the ask is the attribution methodology itself: profiler class per layer, measurement conditions, narrowing loop. Nothing is functionally broken, no single query is named, and no standing telemetry is requested.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke systematic-debugger. The nightly job produces wrong totals about once a week — walk the evidence and find the root cause.
cases.note: SEAM CASE — 'find the root cause' with a BEHAVIOR defect (wrong output) is functional debugging. The profiling skill owns resource/time attribution only; wrong totals are not a where-does-time-go question.
cases.reason: Correctness defects take the hypothesis/reproduction loop of systematic-debugger; no time or memory attribution is involved.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke query-plan-reader. We already know it's this one report query — here's its EXPLAIN ANALYZE output. Tell us what's wrong and how to fix it.
cases.reason: The suspect is evidenced and singular with plan output in hand. Profiling methodology first would be ceremony — the profiling skill's own stop condition routes evidenced suspects directly to the owning skill.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke n-plus-one-detector. The dashboard page fires about 600 nearly identical queries per load according to the query log. Diagnose and design the fix.
cases.reason: Hundreds of near-identical queries per request is the chatty-data-access signature — pattern diagnosis and batching/eager-load design, not time attribution and not single-plan reading.

cases.prompt: Instrument the checkout service with latency histograms and traces, and build the dashboard so we can watch performance continuously.
cases.note: SEAM CASE — continuous instrumentation and dashboards are STANDING telemetry (observability-operator, manual-invocation). Profiling is a bounded, targeted investigation that may CONSUME that telemetry as input.
cases.reason: The deliverable is permanent instrumentation and dashboards, not a bounded attribution investigation with a stop rule.
